diff_summary.content:
# Git hooks are executed by sh, which does not tolerate CRLF line endings.
# Without this pin, a Windows clone with core.autocrlf=true checks the hook
# out with CRLF and it fails at the shebang or on stray \r in every branch.
scripts/githooks/* text eol=lf

More importantly, even granting the Challenger's own hedge that this 'is not evidence of a violation,' the substantive question for C-007 is whether the change weakens enforcement, bypasses verification, or disables logging. A .gitattributes rule that pins LF endings does none of these regardless of which directory it targets: it is strictly a checkout-normalization safeguard. Even if scripts/githooks/ turned out to be a governance-adjacent hook directory, forcing LF line endings makes those hooks MORE reliable, not less enforced.
